endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A continuation announcement with major narrowing may overlap with modification or substitution endpoints; terminal coding should check whether universal fare-free weekends remain in effect.
endpoint_ledger.description: The city formally extends the fare-free weekend policy beyond the initial experiment period, whether as a continued pilot or standing short-term policy.
endpoint_ledger.label: Continue fare-free weekends

meta.important_question: Will city decision-makers continue fare-free weekends beyond the initial experiment window?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Ridership growth and merchant foot-traffic gains create a credible continuation case, but mixed evidence prevents early closure.
realization_criteria: Official city or agency announcement confirms at least one additional scheduled fare-free weekend after evaluation.
No concurrent decision restores standard fares for the same decision window.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario states multiple terminal outcomes are plausible and does not indicate continuation has been decided at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If modifications fully replace universal fare-free weekends with a different pricing regime, substitution endpoint may be the better terminal classification.
endpoint_ledger.description: Officials keep some version of the experiment but materially alter operations, capacity, lines, hours, or scope in response to crowding or budget concerns.
endpoint_ledger.label: Modify experiment

meta.important_question: Will the city materially modify service or scope to address crowding on the two affected lines?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Localized harms often generate corrective design changes rather than all-or-nothing policy reversal.
realization_criteria: Agency or city adopts a documented operational or geographic change tied to the fare-free weekend policy.
Change is justified publicly by crowding, service quality, or cost-management concerns.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Crowding on two lines is explicit and creates a direct mechanism for targeted adjustment without requiring full reversal.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A short pause pending redesign should not count unless officials clearly restore normal fares as the terminal choice.
endpoint_ledger.description: The fare-free weekend experiment ends and standard fare collection resumes without an extension of free weekends.
endpoint_ledger.label: Restore standard fares

meta.important_question: Will officials terminate the experiment and restore standard fares rather than extend or replace it?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Budget pressure and uneven service impacts can produce a conservative reversion to the pre-pilot baseline.
realization_criteria: Official announcement states the experiment is concluded and future weekends will use normal fares.
Fare collection resumes on the relevant services in the next comparable weekend period.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Revenue loss is explicit and creates a plausible rollback path, but the scenario does not indicate termination has occurred.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If targeted discounts are introduced only as a temporary add-on while free weekends continue unchanged, continuation remains the primary endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: Universal fare-free weekends are not continued; instead, leaders adopt a narrower discount, pass, or subsidy mechanism.
endpoint_ledger.label: Replace with targeted affordability program

meta.important_question: Will leaders replace universal fare-free weekends with a narrower discount or subsidy policy?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Substitution is a credible middle path when leaders value access gains but resist recurring revenue loss.
realization_criteria: Formal policy announcement ends or declines universal free weekends and names a targeted affordability alternative.
Alternative pricing or subsidy program is scheduled for implementation or funding.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: The scenario invites multiple terminal outcomes and mixed evidence supports compromise solutions, though no substitute program is yet described.

Decision-makers have not yet chosen a terminal policy path. T0 should preserve uncertainty between continuation, modification, rollback, or substitution.
